case_name: Sarvsheel Mago v State of Haryana and Others

statutes.act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985

facts: The appellant had sought registration of a criminal case against respondents 4-6 for offences under Sections 341, 342, 211 I.P.C. and S.58 of the NDPS Act read with Section 120-B I.P.C.
Nidhi Mago was kidnapped on 15.5.1999 from Chandigarh
She was allegedly made to go through the marriage ceremonies
On 26.5.1999, she was rescued from Golabanda, Orissa and a crime was registered for offences under Sections 376, 363, 366, 468, 467, 471 and I20-B I.P.C.
Nidhi Mago was married to Parshant Arora, son of respondent no.6 on 1.6.1999
Parshant Arora went back to Canada from where he had come and Nidhi Mago was also sent back to her parents' house with the assurance that she will be sent to Canada as soon as her Visa is granted.
In June, 1999, allegedly, there was a dispute among the appellant and respondent no.6 on account of alleged dowry demand
Respondent nos.5 and 6 colluded with each other and started blackmailing the appellant
The Sessions Judge vide his order dated 12.10.2004 was pleased to acquit the appellant and family members of all the charges
Nighi Mago moved an application for maintenance pendente lite against the son of respondent no.6 Parshant Arora, upon which respondent no.6 withdrew petition that he had filed on behalf of his son
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in refusing to issue any direction regarding the registration of a criminal case
Whether the allegations made by the appellant were prima facie true and whether an independent investigation should be conducted into the matter
petitioner_arguments: The appellant had sought registration of a criminal case against respondents 4-6 for offences under Sections 341, 342, 211 I.P.C. and S.58 of the NDPS Act read with Section 120-B I.P.C.
The appellant alleged that respondent no.4 had stopped the vehicle and conducted the search with mala fide motive
The appellant alleged that respondents 5 and 6 colluded with each other and started blackmailing him
respondent_arguments: Respondent no.4 did not find fault with the alleged role played by respondent nos.5 and 6
Respondent no.4 viewed it as a part of the duty of respondent no.4
Respondent no.4 admitted that during the search at Liberty Chowk, Karnal nothing incriminating was found in the car
court_reasoning: The Court is of the opinion that an officer of the rank of DIG under the direct supervision of the DGP should make an independent investigation as to whether any attempt had been made by respondent no.4 herein to harass the petitioner by making endeavours to lodge cases under the NDPS Act
The Court is not oblivious of the fact that the allegations have been made in the light of the disputes between the private parties
holding: The Court grants leave and directs an independent investigation into the matter as directed above
cases_cited: Sarvsheel Mago v State of Haryana
